subject: Geo latency scan & MAP: evaluation plan, benchmarks, and failover playbook
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Derek Simmons <derek.simmons@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kar thik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Geo latency scan & MAP: evaluation plan, benchmarks, and failover playbook

Hi Derek / Monica,

Following our kickoff, attached is a concise MAP and the evaluation plan we discussed. High-level goals:
- Validate regional median/p95 latency and TTFT across US / EU / APAC for your production prompt shapes.
- Measure sustainable throughput and concurrency thresholds per model variant.
- Run multi-region routing + failover experiments (planned failovers: US->EU, EU->APAC) and capture time-to-first-token and error rates.

Proposed timeline (attached MAP worksheet):
1) Apr 12-13: Dataset & prompt set freeze (you provide a 200 prompt seed + 20 edge cases).
2) Apr 15-18: Dry-run single-region profiling (US region) to tune batch / kv-cache settings.
3) Apr 19-22: Parallel regional scans (US/EU/APAC) at target concurrency sweep [1,4,8,16,32].
4) Apr 23: Failover drills + routing policy switch (5x simulated zone outages).
5) Apr 24-25: Results synthesis and close draft (we'll include screenshots and CSVs).

Metrics we'll capture: median latency, p95/p99 latency, TTFT, sustained throughput (req/s), token/sec, error rate, and cold-start penalty during failover. Acceptance thresholds we discussed: p95 < 250ms (US/EU), p95 < 400ms (APAC) at target concurrency of 8; failover RTO target <= 2s to first token (with reduced model if needed).

Please confirm the prompt set delivery on Apr 12 and any additional IP/PSA constraints for APAC traffic. Attached: acme_map_v1.xlsx (MAP worksheet).

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: acme_map_v1.xlsx (MAP worksheet, 3 tabs: milestones, test matrix, contacts)

From: Derek Simmons <derek.simmons@acmecloud.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Park <monica.park@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo latency scan & MAP: evaluation plan, benchmarks, and failover playbook

Thanks Rachel — plan looks good. A couple quick notes:
- We'll deliver the 200 prompt seed + edge cases on Apr 12 by EOD PST.
- For APAC, some traffic must stay in our Singapore VPC during the test window (security req). We'll share a short allowlist.
- For throughput sizing we want sustained token throughput targets: 1.2M tokens/hour peak for the main flows.

One ask: can you include a canary that routes 10% of production traffic to the Redwood hosted endpoint during the Apr 19-22 scans? We want to validate real-world signal in addition to synthetic loads.

If that’s okay, I'll loop in our infra lead (Monica) to coordinate the network allowlist for APAC.

Regards,
Derek
Derek Simmons
Head of Platform Eng, Acme Cloud
derek.simmons@acmecloud.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Kar thik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ACME MAP - run coordination and runbook (dry-run results and ops checklist)

Team — prepping the dry-run this afternoon. Key items for the runbook:
- Test harness: use Redwood internal harness with the prompt corpus from Acme (200 prompts).
- Models: default "rwd-large" and fallback variant "rwd-medium-quant" for failover throttling.
- Concurrency sweep: 1/4/8/16/32; dwell 5 minutes per point; record median/p95/p99 and TTFT.
- Routing: default local region; simulated region outage to trigger routing policy (we'll flip to EU / then APAC).
- Observability: we must snapshot token-level cost and per-request trace ids. Kar thik — please ensure sampling enabled.

Preliminary dry-run (US region, Apr 15 10:30-11:30): attached short result extract. Highlights:
- rwd-large @ concurrency=8: median latency 42ms, p95 178ms, TTFT median 0.12s, sustained throughput 128 req/s.
- At concurrency=32: 400+ ms p95; CPU queueing observed on the instance class (need to cap batching).
- cold-start penalty when spinning up new instances: ~1.1s TTFT to first token (cold kv warmup).

Action items before parallel regional scans:
- Kar thik: tune batching policy to reduce p95 at high concurrency (target: keep p95 < 300ms at 16).
- Soojin: prepare failover script and confirm routing TTLs won't cause long DNS propagation on your side.
- Ben: ensure cost tags and HubSpot metadata capture for each run.

I'll share the full dry-run CSVs after the run completes.

Thanks,
Rachel

Attachment: us_eu_throughput_summary.pdf (dry-run extract)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Kar thik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME MAP - run coordination and runbook (regional sweep complete)

Quick update — regional parallel scans completed (Apr 19-22). I’m attaching the APAC results CSV and a short summary below.

Summary (parallel scan results):
- US (primary): concurrency=8 -> median 45ms, p95 185ms, TTFT median 0.13s, sustained throughput ~120 req/s per N-gpu unit. Errors <0.1%.
- EU: concurrency=8 -> median 60ms, p95 210ms, TTFT 0.16s. Slightly higher due to IP egress path.
- APAC (Singapore): concurrency=8 -> median 95ms, p95 420ms, TTFT median 0.34s. Observed tail spikes during a burst (p99 ~1.2s).

Failover drills (Apr 23):
- US->EU failover: first token observed at ~0.9s for 95% of requests; degraded p95 but successful routing.
- EU->APAC failover: first token ~1.5s; p95 after failover ~550ms. APAC cold caches amplified tail.
- Canary routing at 10%: matched synthetic signal; weighted routing introduced ~5% higher p95 (expected).

Notable operational findings:
- APAC requires an alternate kv-cache priming strategy or a warmed dedicated pool to meet p95 < 400ms at concurrency=8.
- For RTO<2s across all regions we should: 1) deploy a warmed small pooled fleet in APAC, and 2) enable model-fallback to rwd-medium-quant automatically on failover.

Attachments: geo_latency_results_apac.csv

I'll draft a short Playbook section (routing flip steps, expected metrics, rollback) for the MAP deliverable.

— Soojin

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Derek Simmons <derek.simmons@acmecloud.com>, Monica Park <monica.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kar thik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP deliverable: Geo latency scan results + close timeline (next steps & ask)

Derek / Monica — thanks for the collaboration. Attached are the final CSVs and a 1-page synthesis (highlights + recommended actions). TL;DR: we validated the acceptance criteria for US/EU at concurrency 8; APAC shows persistent tail risk without a warmed pool.

Key findings (brief):
- US: p95 185ms at c=8 (PASS).
- EU: p95 210ms at c=8 (PASS, margin limited).
- APAC: p95 420ms at c=8 (FAIL vs target); p99 spikes to ~1.2s during bursts.
- Failover: routing and policy worked; median RTO to first token under 1.5s for most scenarios but exceeded 2s in cold APAC priming.

Recommended MAP updates (actions & owner):
- Short-term (this week): Deploy a warmed mini-pool in APAC (Redwood ops) + enable automatic fallback to rwd-medium-quant on failover (Redwood eng).
- Mid-term (2-4 weeks): Adjust routing policy to prefer regional warm-pools and reduce DNS TTL to 30s for quicker propagation (Acme infra + Redwood).
- Close ask: sign-off on the MAP so we can schedule the warmed pool deployment and roll the canary into 10% production by May 2.

Requested approvals:
- Derek: confirm acceptance to proceed with warmed APAC pool and 10% canary by May 2.
- Monica: confirm network allowlist for Singapore (we received the preliminary list; need final confirmation).

Related artifacts attached: geo_latency_results_apac.csv, us_eu_throughput_summary.pdf, acme_map_v1.xlsx. HubSpot deal updated: https://hubspot.example/record/ACME-4721.

If we get approvals today, I'll open the deployment ticket and draft the MSA addendum for the warmed pool cost (small monthly commitment).

Thanks,
Rachel

Attachment: geo_latency_results_apac.csv; us_eu_throughput_summary.pdf; acme_map_v1.xlsx
